Local Asymptotic Normality

1. Introduction
In regular parametric models, local behavior of the likelihood can be approximated by a Gaussian shift experiment. This approximation supports asymptotic efficiency analysis and clarifies the role of Fisher information.

2. Local Parameterization
Let theta_0 denote the true parameter. Consider local alternatives of the form theta_n = theta_0 + h/sqrt(n), where h is a fixed local direction.

3. Definition of LAN
A sequence of statistical experiments is locally asymptotically normal at theta_0 if the log-likelihood ratio satisfies

log(dP_{theta_0 + h/sqrt(n)}^{(n)} / dP_{theta_0}^{(n)}) = h^T Delta_n - (1/2) h^T I(theta_0) h + o_P(1),

where Delta_n converges in distribution to N(0, I(theta_0)).

4. Central Sequence and Information
The random vector Delta_n is called the central sequence. The matrix I(theta_0) is the Fisher information matrix and captures local curvature of the experiment.

5. Consequences
Under LAN, asymptotically optimal tests and estimators can be derived by studying the corresponding Gaussian shift limit. This yields lower bounds on asymptotic variance and motivates efficient procedures.

6. Summary
LAN provides a unifying asymptotic framework for local inference in regular models.
